text: Surveyor 3 landed on the Moon on April 20, 1967, in the southeastern region of Oceanus Procellarum.
Highly reflective rocks confused the descent radar and the main engine failed to cut off, so the lander bounced twice before it settled.
Its surface sampler could reach up to 1.5 m from the lander and dig up to 18 cm deep.
Tests found the soil had a consistency similar to wet sand and was solid enough to support an Apollo Lunar Module.
Its camera recorded images of an eclipse of the Sun by the Earth.
The eclipse images were taken on April 24, 1967.
note: Date appears on neither NASA page checked.

text: Solar cells generated its power, stored in rechargeable batteries. It failed to come back to life after the two-week lunar night.
Last contact with Surveyor 3 was on May 4, 1967.
safe_text: NASA gives May 4, 1967 as the last contact. Some pages say May 3, the day the Sun set on the lander.
note: NSSDCA: last data 04 May 1967 00:04 UT; operated until after local sunset on 03 May.

text: Apollo 12 astronauts visited Surveyor 3 on November 20, 1969.
safe_text: In November 1969, Apollo 12 astronauts Charles Conrad Jr. and Alan Bean walked to Surveyor 3 and brought parts home, including its TV camera. NASA pages differ on the exact date.
note: Science page: EVA Nov 19, scoop and camera. NSSDCA: 20 November, about 10 kg of parts including the TV camera.
997.9 kg (Science) vs 1026 kg at launch, 296 kg at landing (NSSDCA). No safe wording, so never shown.

text: Apollo 12 photographed Surveyor 3 during its second moonwalk.
An Apollo 12 close-up shows a Surveyor 3 footpad and the surface sampler with its scoop.
One Apollo 12 photograph shows two spacecraft on the Moon: Surveyor 3 in the foreground and the Lunar Module in the background.
